findings.issue: In-memory cache is unbounded: entries (including cached null 404s for arbitrary user-supplied resource names) are never evicted, only replaced on access; memory grows for the life of the process.
findings.suggestion: Add a size cap (LRU) or a periodic sweep of expired entries alongside the existing TTL check.

findings.issue: Every page downloads all five islands' JS because the document imports them globally, defeating Gracile's per-route client bundle splitting.
findings.suggestion: Move island imports to per-route routes/*.client.ts entrypoints (e.g. (home).client.ts imports pokemon-browser, pokemon/[name].client.ts imports moves-panel/sortable-table/team-toggle).

findings.issue: isBuildRender couples to the engine's internal 'gracile-static' stub hostname; correct for @gracile/engine 0.11.0 (verified) but an undocumented internal with no stability contract.
findings.suggestion: Keep the helper but reference the engine version/behavior in the comment and add a build-time smoke test that would catch a hostname change.

findings.issue: Module-global AbortController shared by pokemon-browser, moves-panel and team-page; two fetching islands on the same page would silently cancel each other's in-flight fragment loads.
findings.suggestion: Create one AbortController per island instance (per #load call) instead of a module singleton.

findings.issue: No timeout on the upstream PokeAPI fetch; a hung request occupies a concurrency slot (and the caller) indefinitely.
findings.suggestion: Wrap fetch with AbortSignal.timeout(...) (a few seconds) and let the existing failure-eviction path clean up.

findings.issue: Out-of-range ?page= is clamped to the last page while the URL keeps the bogus value, so the URL and rendered content disagree.
findings.suggestion: Redirect (or replaceState) to the clamped page's URL, or render 404 for out-of-range pages.

findings.issue: popstate listener registered in connectedCallback with no disconnectedCallback teardown.
findings.suggestion: Track the handler and remove it in disconnectedCallback (cheap insurance given fragment replacement happens nearby).

findings.issue: The slot-sorted type-badge mapping (sort by slot, label via typeLabels ?? humanize) is duplicated in data.ts (getTeamCards, getMoveTables) and in routes/pokemon/[name].ts:65 and routes/moves/[name].ts:32.
findings.suggestion: Extract a typesToBadges(types, labels) helper in data.ts next to TypeBadge and use it everywhere.

findings.issue: Asset hrefs computed at runtime via new URL('./styles/app.css', import.meta.url).pathname inject machine-specific absolute filesystem paths into the prerendered HTML; they only work because the engine strips and re-injects server assets in server output.
findings.suggestion: Use the documented root-relative string paths (e.g. href="/src/styles/app.css") so the emitted HTML is position-independent.

findings.issue: lit is declared as a direct dependency but never imported: islands are vanilla custom elements and SSR html comes from @gracile/gracile/server-html.
findings.suggestion: Either rewrite the islands as LitElement components (the 'Gracile with Lit' flavor) or drop the unused direct dependency.

summary: A genuinely well-built Gracile app on the current stable release: idiomatic route/document/adapter patterns, a clean server/client boundary, deliberate 404, escaping and race handling, and a team-builder feature that reuses the existing conventions rather than bolting on new ones. The blockers are minor: an unbounded API cache, all client JS shipped on every page instead of per-route entrypoints, and a couple of robustness nits (shared abort controller, no fetch timeout). I'd merge after one small round of changes.
